verification_report.summary:
The supplied proof is correct relative to the explicitly accepted inputs. All statements were checked in textual order, including the actual hypotheses of the internal references. This verdict does not independently certify smooth_second_estimate_01, compactness_regularization_01, bounded_comparison_01 or local_contacts_01, and excludes the unbounded reduction.

The smooth existence argument has the correct extrema bounds, invertible linearization L_u-lambda, and an open-and-closed continuity path. The accepted semilinear estimates apply for fixed lambda and uniformly smooth forcing tF. Smooth comparison has the correct sign: determinant >= exponential supplies a lower subsolution. Uniqueness follows from the same maximum argument.

For smooth obstacles, the upper obstacle bound and the shifted strict subsolution give p-delta-C_j/beta <= u_beta <= p+C_f/beta. Continuity and decreasing regularization justify Dini convergence. Choosing delta, then fixing j, then sending beta to infinity permits arbitrarily fast decay of c_j. No derivative bound uniform in beta is needed. Uniform convergence and exponential decay away from contact establish smooth-obstacle support.

Continuous obstacle approximation is valid. For lower semicontinuous obstacles, infimal convolution increases pointwise with common bounds; the regularized increasing envelope limit lies below f quasi-everywhere. Portmanteau on the open sets {p_infinity<f_k} has the correct direction. Hermitian domination applies with c=0, u=p_infinity and v=P_omega(f), identifying the limit without circularity.

The exceptional-set construction produces lower semicontinuous approximants, including at boundary points: the inside value M is at least the continuous complementary value. Decreasing tail unions ensure monotonicity, quasi-everywhere convergence and capacity convergence. Fixed quasi-continuous coefficients pass through the bounded-product limits by continuous extension off small-capacity sets and uniform capacity control.

For semipositive theta, constant competitors give common bounds and nested competitor classes identify the decreasing envelope limit. With Omega=theta+omega, expansion of (Omega+ddc p_j-(1-1/j)omega)^n proves weak convergence in a fixed background. Positivity also bounds these measures by (Omega+ddc p_j)^n, providing the uniform capacity control needed for the same test coefficients. These are bounds for a common bounded range, not BMP. No bigness, PVP or positive limiting mass is required.

The source attribution is accurate: GL22 uses stronger C1,1 estimates in its smooth step, whereas the supplied replacement derives the needed convergence from the accepted inputs. The envelope convention and relevant hypotheses agree. [GL22, Theorem 2.3](https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf).
